title: A febrile infant 8 to 21 days old is admitted
lead: A well-appearing infant 8 to 21 days old with a fever of 38.0°C or higher gets urine, blood, and cerebrospinal fluid cultures and parenteral antibiotics in the hospital.
lines: This is not an outpatient viral visit.
The AAP 2021 guideline is the source of that age band.
Do not subtract the rectal temperature because the baby looks calm.
miss: Sending a 2-week-old with a fever of 38.2 home with a virus explanation.

source.name: AAP Clinical Practice Guideline. Evaluation and Management of Well-Appearing Febrile Infants 8 to 60 Days Old.
source.says: Infants 8 to 21 days old are hospitalized for a full culture evaluation and parenteral antibiotics.

title: A newborn of a mother with diabetes is fed and the glucose is checked
lead: A newborn whose mother had diabetes is fed early and the glucose is checked. The baby's insulin is still high after the cord is cut.
lines: Jitteriness is a low glucose until proved otherwise.
Do not wait for a seizure to check.
The mother's control during pregnancy is the history you ask for.
miss: Discharging a jittery infant of a diabetic mother at 6 hours without a glucose.

source.name: StatPearls. Gestational Diabetes.
source.says: Neonatal hypoglycemia is anticipated and checked. Early feeding is the first prevention.

title: A Turner girl's blood pressure is measured in the arm and the leg
lead: At every visit for Turner syndrome, compare the arm and the leg blood pressure and listen for the aortic valve. The karyotype result is not a completed plan.
lines: A new gradient is imaging, not a year of observation.
Growth hormone and estrogen are timed with a specialist, not started casually.
Renal ultrasound is done if it was never done.
miss: Refilling a note that says Turner and never taking a leg pressure.

source.name: StatPearls. Turner Syndrome.
source.says: Ongoing care includes blood-pressure comparison and cardiac surveillance for coarctation and bicuspid aortic valve.

title: Salt-wasting adrenal crisis in an infant is steroid and saline first
lead: A vomiting, shocked infant in the first weeks of life gets a glucose, a sodium, a potassium, and a stress-dose steroid. The genital exam does not delay the steroid.
lines: Hyponatremia and hyperkalemia are the lab pair.
17-hydroxyprogesterone is sent. The result is not required to treat.
Do not give only antibiotics.
miss: Fluid-resuscitating a shocked neonate and waiting a day for the newborn screen.

source.name: StatPearls. Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
source.says: Salt-wasting crisis is treated with stress-dose glucocorticoid and saline immediately. The diagnostic steroid precursor is sent, not awaited.

title: The first sickle-cell pain order is incentive spirometry
lead: For a sickle-cell pain crisis, write incentive spirometry on admission. It prevents acute chest syndrome while you treat the pain.
lines: Oxygen is for hypoxia, not for a saturation of 99%.
Fluids are enough to correct deficit, not a flood.
A new infiltrate changes the admission to acute chest syndrome.
miss: Admitting for morphine without a spirometer or a plan to walk.

source.name: StatPearls. Sickle Cell Disease.
source.says: Incentive spirometry is ordered for vaso-occlusive pain admissions because it reduces acute chest syndrome.

title: Exchange transfusion is the order for severe acute chest or stroke
lead: Severe acute chest syndrome or an acute stroke in sickle cell disease is an exchange-transfusion call, not another unit of simple transfusion as the whole plan.
lines: Simple transfusion is for symptomatic anemia.
Call the blood bank early. The exchange takes time to arrange.
Hydroxyurea is the outpatient prevention, not the drug that treats today's stroke.
miss: Ordering one unit of packed cells and a neurology clinic visit for an acute ischemic stroke in sickle cell disease.

source.name: StatPearls. Sickle Cell Disease.
source.says: Exchange transfusion is used for severe acute chest syndrome and acute stroke. Simple transfusion does not replace it.

title: Plasma exchange is ordered before the ADAMTS13 returns
lead: When the smear and the story are thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, order plasma exchange now. The ADAMTS13 result confirms later.
lines: Do not platelet-transfuse unless there is life-threatening bleeding.
Hold the platelet-making argument and start the exchange.
Daily labs follow the lactate dehydrogenase and the platelets.
miss: Waiting for the send-out ADAMTS13 before calling the apheresis service.

source.name: StatPearls. Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura.
source.says: Plasma exchange is started on clinical grounds. Platelet transfusion is reserved for life-threatening bleeding.

title: Febrile neutropenia: antibiotic within the hour, vancomycin only if indicated
lead: Write the antipseudomonal antibiotic as a stat order. Add vancomycin only for instability, a line infection, severe mucositis, or known resistant gram-positive colonization.
lines: Cultures are drawn if they do not delay the drug.
A stable patient does not need three extra antibiotics.
The source, including the perianal exam, is looked at.
miss: Ordering vancomycin, metronidazole, and an antifungal with the first fever in a stable patient.

source.name: StatPearls. Febrile Neutropenia.
source.says: Antipseudomonal therapy is immediate. Vancomycin is added for specific indications, not for every fever.

title: A head bleed in hemophilia is factor first, scan second
lead: A hemophilia patient with head trauma gets factor replacement immediately. The CT does not come before the factor.
lines: Aim for a full correction for a central-nervous-system bleed.
Do not give an intramuscular injection.
An inhibitor is suspected when the bleed does not stop with the usual dose.
miss: Sending the patient to CT while the factor is still in the pharmacy.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemophilia A.
source.says: Factor replacement for suspected intracranial bleeding is immediate and is not delayed for imaging.

title: Stop heparin in all its forms when HIT is suspected
lead: When heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is suspected, discontinue every heparin product, including flushes and coated catheters, and order a non-heparin anticoagulant.
lines: Write the allergy so the next shift does not restart a flush.
Do not order warfarin tonight.
Send the antibody, but do not wait for it to stop the drug.
miss: Changing the heparin drip to a heparin flush and calling that a stop.

source.name: StatPearls. Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.
source.says: All heparin exposures stop at suspicion. A non-heparin anticoagulant is ordered the same hour.

title: Cryoprecipitate is the fibrinogen order in DIC
lead: In a bleeding patient with DIC and a low fibrinogen, order cryoprecipitate. Ordering only fresh frozen plasma does not reliably replace fibrinogen.
lines: The cause, the sepsis or the abruption or the leukemia, is ordered at the same time.
Platelets are for the bleeding patient, not for a standing daily threshold.
Recheck the fibrinogen after the product.
miss: Ordering a unit of red cells and no fibrinogen for a patient whose fibrinogen is 70.

source.name: StatPearls. Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation.
source.says: Cryoprecipitate replaces fibrinogen in bleeding DIC. Product replacement does not replace treatment of the cause.

title: Rasburicase is a stat order, and the uric acid tube is special
lead: If you give rasburicase, the uric-acid sample has to be handled so the drug does not keep working in the tube and fake a low result.
lines: Fluids are already running.
The potassium is on a monitor and a repeat lab.
G6PD deficiency is the contraindication you ask about.
miss: Celebrating a uric acid of 1 drawn in a warm tube after rasburicase.

source.name: StatPearls. Tumor Lysis Syndrome.
source.says: Rasburicase continues to degrade uric acid in the specimen unless the sample is handled correctly. The potassium is followed separately.

title: Phlebotomy for polycythemia vera has a hematocrit target
lead: Order phlebotomy for polycythemia vera toward a hematocrit under 45%, and do not apply that target to a hypoxic patient with a high erythropoietin.
lines: Aspirin is added when the diagnosis is secure.
Hydroxyurea is for the high-risk patient, written as a planned drug, not a one-time dose.
Tell the patient to report erythromelalgia and clots.
miss: Phlebotomizing a patient with COPD and a high EPO down to a hematocrit of 40.

source.name: StatPearls. Polycythemia Vera.
source.says: Phlebotomy targets a hematocrit below 45% in polycythemia vera and is not the treatment of secondary erythrocytosis.

title: ATRA is a now order, and the fibrinogen is checked twice a shift
lead: For suspected acute promyelocytic leukemia, order all-trans retinoic acid and a fibrinogen now, and recheck the fibrinogen on the same shift.
lines: The blood bank knows this patient can bleed.
Differentiation syndrome is fever and infiltrates after the drug. Do not call it pneumonia and stop the drug without a specialist.
The genetic test is sent. It is not the start time.
miss: Scheduling the bone-marrow biopsy for Monday and the drug for after the result.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
source.says: All-trans retinoic acid and coagulopathy monitoring start when the diagnosis is suspected, not when genetics return.

title: Vaccinate before or as you start a complement inhibitor
lead: Before or as a complement inhibitor starts for PNH, order meningococcal vaccination. The drug blocks the defense against Neisseria.
lines: The hemolysis drug is not delayed for a life-threatening clot, and the vaccine is not forgotten.
Iron is replaced if the urine has been losing it.
Anticoagulation alone is not the whole plan.
miss: Starting eculizumab on Friday and leaving the vaccine for a clinic that does not exist.

source.name: StatPearls. Paroxysmal Nocturnal Hemoglobinuria.
source.says: Complement inhibition requires meningococcal vaccination because terminal-complement defense is blocked.

title: A transfusion reaction order is stop, keep, and send
lead: The order set for a suspected hemolytic reaction is: stop the transfusion, keep the bag and tubing, send a new sample, and do not restart that unit.
lines: Normal saline is the fluid. More blood is a new decision.
Check the name on the bag against the wristband yourself.
Urine output and pressure are the bedside monitors.
miss: Slowing the rate to 10 mL an hour and leaving the same unit hanging.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction.
source.says: The unit is stopped and returned with a new specimen. It is not restarted.

title: Myeloma hypercalcemia is saline, and the bone is protected
lead: Severe hypercalcemia from myeloma is saline first. A bisphosphonate is ordered for the bone disease, not as the only drug in a dehydrated patient.
lines: The light chains need a urine or serum free-light-chain test, not an albumin dipstick.
Infection is common. A fever is cultured.
Thalidomide-era steroids are a specialist regimen. Fluids are yours tonight.
miss: Giving a bisphosphonate and no fluid to a creatinine of 3.

source.name: StatPearls. Multiple Myeloma.
source.says: Volume resuscitation treats the hypercalcemia of myeloma. Antiresorptive therapy is added for bone disease after the patient is moving urine.

title: Aplastic anemia transfusions are limited if transplant is possible
lead: In a young patient with aplastic anemia who may be transplanted, transfuse for symptoms and avoid blood from family donors, who can sensitize the recipient.
lines: The marrow is the diagnostic test and is ordered, not inferred.
Infection precautions are written.
Growth factors are not a substitute for a diagnosis.
miss: Transfusing a sibling's directed donation the night before a transplant evaluation.

source.name: StatPearls. Aplastic Anemia.
source.says: Transfusions are minimized and family-donor blood is avoided when hematopoietic transplant is a possibility.

title: Blood pressure before a thrombolytic is under 185/110
lead: Before alteplase or tenecteplase, the blood pressure is brought under 185/110. If you are not giving a reperfusion drug and the pressure is under 220/120, do not lower it in the first two days.
lines: Write the thrombolytic only after the pressure is in range and the exclusion list is checked.
A patient who is not reperfused is harmed by an aggressive pressure drop.
Recheck the pressure after the drug. The target while the infusion's risk window is open is lower still, under about 180/105.
miss: Lowering a pressure of 190/100 in a patient who is not getting a thrombolytic, or giving the drug at 200/115.

source.name: 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke.
source.says: Trial protocols required pressure under 185/110 before thrombolysis. Without reperfusion, lowering pressure under 220/120 in the first 48 to 72 hours does not help.

title: The stroke order is a finger-stick and a CT before the drug
lead: The first stroke orders are a glucose, a noncontrast CT, and a clock. Hypoglycemia copies a stroke and is treated, not lysed.
lines: The CT excludes hemorrhage. It does not have to show the infarct.
Do not delay the drug inside 4.5 hours for an MRI.
A swallow screen is ordered before the first meal.
miss: Sending the patient to MRI and giving breakfast before a swallow screen.

source.name: 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke.
source.says: Glucose and noncontrast CT precede thrombolysis. MRI is not required inside the standard window.

title: Status epilepticus orders: glucose, benzo, then one full second drug
lead: The status order is a glucose, a benzodiazepine now, and if it continues one full dose of levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, or valproate.
lines: Do not stack quarter-doses of lorazepam.
Protect the airway while the drugs are drawn.
A benzodiazepine level or a neurology consult is not the first order.
miss: Starting a phenytoin load and never giving the benzodiazepine.

source.name: StatPearls. Status Epilepticus.
source.says: Glucose is checked, a benzodiazepine is given immediately, and one adequate second-line dose follows if seizures continue.

title: A thunderclap order is CT now, and a plan if it is negative
lead: Order a noncontrast head CT before any migraine drug for a headache that peaked at onset. If it is negative in the first hours, order the next test rather than a discharge.
lines: The next test is a lumbar puncture or a vascular study, chosen by timing.
Do not give a triptan to a headache you have not cleared.
Document the time the pain became maximal.
miss: Discharging a negative CT at hour two with a sumatriptan prescription.

source.name: StatPearls. Thunderclap Headache.
source.says: CT is immediate. A negative early CT does not complete the exclusion of subarachnoid hemorrhage.

title: Meningitis: steroid and drug before the scanner if you must scan
lead: If a CT is required before the lumbar puncture, the dexamethasone and the antibiotic are given first. The puncture happens after the scan.
lines: Blood cultures are drawn if they do not delay the drug.
The steroid is with the first dose when pneumococcus is likely.
A normal CT does not mean you skip the puncture.
miss: Holding the antibiotic until the patient returns from CT and the puncture is done.

source.name: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Management of Bacterial Meningitis.
source.says: Antibiotics and dexamethasone are not delayed for imaging. The lumbar puncture follows the scan when a scan is required.

title: Watch the numbers that say the diaphragm is failing
lead: In Guillain-Barré syndrome, order vital capacity and negative inspiratory force on a schedule. Intubate when those numbers fall, not when the patient arrests.
lines: A rising CO2 is late.
IVIG or exchange is ordered the day you make the diagnosis.
Steroids are not on the order set.
miss: Checking a chest film instead of a vital capacity.

source.name: StatPearls. Guillain-Barre Syndrome.
source.says: Serial respiratory mechanics detect diaphragm failure early. Immunoglobulin or exchange is ordered, and steroids are not.

title: A multiple-sclerosis admission includes a search for infection
lead: Before you order a high-dose steroid for a supposed flare, order a search for infection. A urinary infection can revive old symptoms.
lines: MRI is for a new deficit, not for every warm day.
The disease-modifying drug is reconciled so it is not missed at discharge.
Fever itself is treated.
miss: Starting methylprednisolone for a positive urine culture and old leg weakness.

source.name: StatPearls. Multiple Sclerosis.
source.says: Pseudo-relapse from infection is excluded before a flare is treated with corticosteroids.

title: Parkinson medications are given on the patient's clock
lead: In the hospital, order carbidopa-levodopa at the patient's home times. A missed dose causes rigidity that looks like a new illness.
lines: Do not order a dopamine blocker for nausea.
A swallowing evaluation is ordered if the doses are being missed because of dysphagia.
Fall precautions are written.
miss: Holding all Parkinson drugs because the patient is NPO for a test that could have been timed.

source.name: StatPearls. Parkinson Disease.
source.says: Home timing of levodopa is continued in the hospital. Dopamine-blocking antiemetics are avoided.

title: Cord compression: dexamethasone and MRI today
lead: Order dexamethasone and an MRI today for back pain with leg weakness, a sensory level, or new urinary retention. The oncology staging can wait.
lines: Radiation oncology or spine surgery is called when the MRI confirms compression.
Plain films are not the test.
A bladder scan documents the retention.
miss: Scheduling the MRI for next week and a clinic visit.

source.name: StatPearls. Spinal Cord Compression.
source.says: Dexamethasone and same-day MRI are the orders. Decompression is arranged from the result.

title: A TIA leaves with a drug and a monitored plan
lead: A TIA discharge order includes an antithrombotic, a statin if atherosclerotic disease is the cause, and a follow-up measured in days, not months.
lines: If atrial fibrillation is found, the drug is an anticoagulant, not aspirin.
Carotid imaging is ordered before or immediately after discharge.
Driving and the next symptom are written in the instructions.
miss: Discharging on aspirin with a neurology appointment in three months and no carotid study.

source.name: StatPearls. Transient Ischemic Attack.
source.says: Antithrombotic therapy and urgent vascular and cardiac evaluation are the discharge plan.

title: Horner syndrome imaging is ordered the day you see it
lead: Order vascular imaging the day you diagnose a painful Horner syndrome. A chest image that includes the apex is added for a smoker.
lines: Do not schedule it as a routine outpatient study next month.
Neurologic signs beyond the eye move the patient to a stroke pathway.
Document which pupil is small.
miss: Referring to ophthalmology in two weeks for a painful drooping lid.

source.name: StatPearls. Horner Syndrome.
source.says: Acute painful Horner syndrome is imaged the same day for dissection. The lung apex is included when smoking is the history.

title: Migraine discharge is a limit on painkillers
lead: A migraine discharge names the acute drug, the limit per week, and the red flags that mean come back. Daily painkillers create the next headache.
lines: Do not prescribe a triptan and an opioid together as the plan.
A first headache after age 50 is not labeled migraine without a thought.
Pregnancy status is checked before the drug.
miss: Refilling a daily combination analgesic and a triptan with no limit.

source.name: StatPearls. Migraine Headache.
source.says: Discharge instructions limit acute medication frequency to prevent medication-overuse headache and name the reasons to return.

title: Delirium orders remove the cause and the anticholinergic
lead: The delirium order set looks for infection, drugs, urine retention, and constipation, and it stops diphenhydramine. A benzodiazepine is not the treatment unless the cause is alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal.
lines: Glasses and hearing aids are ordered back to the bedside.
A sitter is safer than a restraint.
The family is told this is often reversible.
miss: Ordering lorazepam every six hours for an older patient who is confused after a hip fracture.

source.name: StatPearls. Differentiating Delirium Versus Dementia in Older Adults.
source.says: Delirium is treated by removing the cause and deliriogenic drugs. Benzodiazepines are reserved for withdrawal.

title: A brain abscess order is antibiotics and a surgeon, not a lumbar puncture
lead: Order antibiotics that cover the source and a surgical consult. Do not order a lumbar puncture as the diagnostic test.
lines: CT or MRI is the image.
The ear, the sinus, and the heart are examined.
A small abscess in a stable patient can be antibiotics and a short-interval scan, written as a plan.
miss: Ordering a lumbar puncture for a ring-enhancing lesion with a midline shift.

source.name: StatPearls. Brain Abscess.
source.says: Imaging, source-directed antibiotics, and surgical consultation are the orders. Lumbar puncture is avoided.

title: Lithium admission: hold, hydrate, and a level timed correctly
lead: Hold lithium, start saline if the patient is dry, and time the level so you do not sample during the distribution phase and undercall the toxicity.
lines: Stop the NSAID or the thiazide that raised it.
Dialysis is ordered for severe neurotoxicity, not for a mild tremor.
The home dose is not restarted at discharge without a new level and a reason.
miss: Restarting the home dose the next morning because the patient looks better.

source.name: StatPearls. Lithium Toxicity.
source.says: Lithium is held, volume is restored, interacting drugs are stopped, and dialysis is reserved for severe toxicity.

title: Serotonin syndrome: stop the new drug tonight
lead: The order is to discontinue every serotonergic drug on tonight's list, including the linezolid or the tramadol that was just added.
lines: A benzodiazepine is ordered for agitation.
Cyproheptadine is ordered if supportive care is failing.
Cooling is ordered if the temperature is high. Restraints alone are not.
miss: Continuing the SSRI and adding another dose of tramadol for the shivering.

source.name: StatPearls. Serotonin Syndrome.
source.says: All serotonergic agents are stopped immediately. Benzodiazepines and cooling are the supportive orders.

title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: stop the drug and check the CK
lead: Discontinue the antipsychotic and order a creatine kinase, a temperature, and cooling. Do not order another dose for agitation.
lines: Fluids are ordered because the muscle is breaking down.
A benzodiazepine may be ordered for agitation.
The drug is not restarted this admission.
miss: Ordering haloperidol for the rigidity.

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
source.says: The antagonist is stopped, creatine kinase and temperature are monitored, and cooling and fluids are ordered.

title: Bell palsy discharge is a steroid and an eye-care plan
lead: Discharge Bell palsy with a corticosteroid started today and instructions to lubricate the eye that does not close, including at night.
lines: Forehead sparing cancels the discharge and starts a stroke evaluation.
Ear vesicles change the drug plan to include antiviral therapy for zoster.
Tell the patient when to return if the eye hurts.
miss: Discharging without eye protection because the smile is the complaint.

source.name: StatPearls. Bell Palsy.
source.says: Early corticosteroids and corneal protection are the discharge plan. Forehead sparing is not discharged as Bell palsy.

title: A cerebellar bleed is a surgical call, not a floor admission
lead: Admit a cerebellar hemorrhage to a setting that can operate, and call neurosurgery when you order the CT, not the next morning.
lines: Blood pressure orders follow hemorrhagic-stroke practice and avoid overcorrection.
Reverse anticoagulation if it is present.
A falling level of consciousness is an immediate call, not a note.
miss: Admitting a cerebellar hemorrhage to a medical floor with neuro checks every 8 hours.

source.name: StatPearls. Hemorrhagic Stroke Overview.
source.says: Cerebellar hemorrhage is admitted where evacuation can happen. Neurosurgery is involved at diagnosis.

title: Epidural hematoma: reverse, type and screen, operating room
lead: The orders for a deteriorating epidural hematoma are reversal of anticoagulation, a type and screen, and the operating room.
lines: Serial exams are for a stable patient a neurosurgeon has accepted for observation.
The lucid interval is documented so the next clinician knows the course.
Do not send the patient off the monitor for a nonurgent test.
miss: Observing a dilating pupil on a medical ward.

source.name: StatPearls. Epidural Hematoma.
source.says: Deterioration triggers reversal, blood availability, and evacuation. Observation is only for a stable, accepted patient.

title: Subdural hematoma discharge is a reversed anticoagulant and a plan
lead: If a small subdural hematoma is discharged or observed, the anticoagulant is reversed and a written plan says when it may restart and who rechecks the scan.
lines: A shift or a worsening exam cancels the discharge.
Fall precautions and a caregiver are named.
The indication for the anticoagulant, such as a mechanical valve, changes the restart and is not ignored.
miss: Restarting the DOAC that night because the patient is in atrial fibrillation and the scan was small.

source.name: StatPearls. Subdural Hematoma.
source.says: Anticoagulation is reversed and restarted only under a plan. Mass effect or worsening cancels observation.

title: Compartment syndrome: remove the cast and call surgery in one order
lead: The order is to bivalve or remove the cast and to call the surgeon for fasciotomy. Analgesia is given and does not replace the call.
lines: Document pain with passive stretch.
A present pulse is written down so nobody waits for it to vanish.
The limb is kept at the level of the heart, not dangling and not forgotten.
miss: Increasing the morphine and leaving the tight cast on until morning rounds.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Compartment Syndrome and Fasciotomy.
source.says: External compression is removed immediately and fasciotomy is arranged. Analgesia is adjunctive.

title: Hip fracture orders: pain, prophylaxis, and a surgical date
lead: Write pain control, venous-thromboembolism prophylaxis, and a surgical plan within about 48 hours for a medically ready hip fracture.
lines: Delirium precautions are on the order set: no diphenhydramine, glasses on, catheter out.
A fragility fracture gets an osteoporosis treatment plan before discharge.
Consent and the medical issues that truly delay surgery are listed, not a vague clearance.
miss: Waiting five days for every consultant to say the word cleared.

source.name: StatPearls. Hip Fracture Overview.
source.says: Early surgery, analgesia, and clot prophylaxis are the admission orders. Osteoporosis treatment is arranged before discharge.

title: Open fracture: antibiotics and tetanus are stat
lead: An open fracture order is a stat antibiotic, a tetanus update, a sterile dressing, and the operating room for irrigation.
lines: The antibiotic spectrum follows how dirty the wound is.
Do not close the wound in the emergency department.
A photo and a neurovascular exam are documented before the dressing hides them.
miss: Splinting and arranging antibiotics with the morning surgical add-on list.

source.name: StatPearls. Open Fracture Management.
source.says: Antibiotics and tetanus prophylaxis are immediate. Operative irrigation is the wound plan.

title: Septic knee: tap, then wash, then narrow the drug
lead: Order the aspiration before the antibiotic if the patient is stable, then surgical washout, then narrow the antibiotic to the culture.
lines: A prosthetic joint is a different order: do not start a short oral course.
Gonorrhea swabs are added when the history fits.
Weight-bearing status is written so the joint is protected.
miss: Discharging a hot prosthetic knee on oral cephalexin.

source.name: StatPearls. Septic Arthritis.
source.says: Aspiration precedes antibiotics in stable patients. Washout and culture-directed antibiotics follow.

title: Gout flare orders name one anti-inflammatory and the kidney
lead: Order one anti-inflammatory the kidneys allow: an NSAID, colchicine, or a steroid. Do not order allopurinol as the only drug.
lines: If the patient already takes allopurinol, continue it.
Check the creatinine before the NSAID.
Tell the patient the flare drug is not the uric-acid drug.
miss: Starting allopurinol alone and an opioid for a hot toe.

source.name: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout.
source.says: The flare is treated with an anti-inflammatory. Allopurinol monotherapy is not flare treatment.

title: Back pain without a flag goes home without an MRI
lead: Discharge acute low back pain without a red flag with activity and no MRI. Write the flags that should bring the patient back.
lines: Cauda equina symptoms cancel the discharge and start an MRI today.
Opioids are not the default prescription.
Work advice is to move, not to stay in bed.
miss: Ordering an MRI for two days of pain and prescribing bed rest.

source.name: ACP Clinical Practice Guideline. Noninvasive Treatments for Acute, Subacute, and Chronic Low Back Pain.
source.says: Imaging is not ordered in the first weeks without red flags. Activity is advised.

title: Giant-cell arteritis: steroid tonight, biopsy this week
lead: Order high-dose glucocorticoid tonight if vision is threatened, and schedule the temporal-artery biopsy within days so the histology is not lost.
lines: Do not wait for the sedimentation rate.
Ask about the other eye and the jaw.
The biopsy is not cancelled because the steroid has started.
miss: Scheduling the biopsy in three weeks and the steroid after the result.

source.name: StatPearls. Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).
source.says: Glucocorticoids start immediately when vision is at risk. Biopsy is arranged promptly and is not delayed by treatment.

title: Necrotizing fasciitis orders are the operating room and broad antibiotics
lead: Write an operating-room booking and broad antibiotics at the same time. Do not write a 24-hour trial.
lines: Mark the skin so spread is visible.
Surgery is called by name, not as a routine consult for the morning.
Fluids and a lactate are ordered because these patients are in shock.
miss: Admitting to medicine for intravenous cefazolin and a surgery consult in the morning.

source.name: StatPearls. Necrotizing Fasciitis.
source.says: Immediate operative debridement and broad antibiotics are ordered together.

title: Ankylosing spondylitis discharge is an NSAID and an eye warning
lead: Discharge with an NSAID, a plan to stay active, and instructions to seek care the same day for a red painful eye.
lines: A TNF inhibitor is a follow-up decision, not the emergency-department start.
Do not prescribe prolonged bed rest.
Chest pain in this disease can be aortitis and is not ignored.
miss: Prescribing two weeks of bed rest and no warning about the eye.

source.name: StatPearls. Ankylosing Spondylitis.
source.says: NSAIDs and activity are the discharge treatment. Acute uveitis is a same-day return precaution.

title: Marfan discharge includes an aortic-imaging appointment
lead: A new Marfan diagnosis is discharged with a dated aortic-imaging appointment and a blood-pressure plan, not with reassurance about height.
lines: Pregnancy counseling is written if it applies.
Contact-sport restriction is written if the aorta is dilated.
A beta blocker or an angiotensin-receptor blocker is the medication conversation.
miss: Telling the patient the click is benign and scheduling nothing.

source.name: StatPearls. Marfan Syndrome.
source.says: Aortic imaging and blood-pressure treatment are arranged. Activity and pregnancy counseling are part of the plan.

title: Pemphigus admission is fluids, wound care, and a steroid
lead: Order fluids, wound care, and systemic steroids for widespread pemphigus. The mouth is inspected so the patient can actually drink.
lines: Infection of denuded skin is watched.
A steroid-sparing drug is a follow-up, not a reason to delay the steroid.
Bullous pemphigoid is not given the same intensity by reflex.
miss: Discharging widespread skin loss with a topical cream.

source.name: StatPearls. Pemphigus Vulgaris.
source.says: Widespread disease needs systemic steroids, fluids, and wound care. Oral involvement affects hydration.

title: Dermatomyositis discharge includes a cancer-screening plan
lead: An adult with new dermatomyositis leaves with immunosuppression started or arranged and a written cancer-screening plan.
lines: Breathlessness gets imaging before discharge if it is new.
The steroid is not the whole plan if the weakness is severe.
A statin is stopped if it is a possible contributor, and the rash is still explained.
miss: Prescribing prednisone with no follow-up and no cancer plan.

source.name: StatPearls. Dermatomyositis.
source.says: Immunosuppression is started and malignancy screening is arranged for adult disease.

title: Chest-pain orders: ECG, aspirin, and oxygen only if hypoxic
lead: The first chest-pain orders are an ECG within 10 minutes, aspirin if it is safe, and oxygen only if the saturation is low.
lines: A STEMI activates the lab before the troponin.
Two large IVs are ordered if reperfusion or instability is likely.
A normal first ECG with ongoing pain gets a repeat, not a discharge.
miss: Waiting for a bed assignment to obtain the ECG.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: ECG within 10 minutes and aspirin are the opening orders. Routine oxygen is omitted when saturation is normal.

title: A STEMI transfer is a clock you write down
lead: When a STEMI presents at a hospital that cannot do PCI, write the transfer time goal of 120 minutes or give a fibrinolytic if that goal will be missed.
lines: Activate the receiving lab before the ambulance leaves.
Do not wait for the troponin to decide.
Document first medical contact, not just door time.
miss: Holding the patient for a morning catheterization slot at a hospital two hours away.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: Transfer PCI is acceptable within 120 minutes. If that cannot be met, fibrinolysis is given.

title: Heart-failure discharge starts the missing pillar
lead: Before a HFrEF discharge, start any of the four pillars that are missing and safe, and book follow-up within 7 days.
lines: The 2024 hospitalized-heart-failure pathway emphasizes starting them in the hospital.
A small creatinine rise is not a stop order on the discharge summary.
Daily weights and the salt plan are written in words the patient can use.
miss: Discharging on a loop diuretic alone with a clinic visit in six weeks.

source.name: 2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway for Patients Hospitalized With Heart Failure.
source.says: All four pillars are started before discharge when possible, and follow-up is within about 7 days.

title: Improved ejection fraction is continued on the discharge list
lead: The discharge list for improved ejection fraction keeps the HFrEF drugs. Write do not stop on the summary.
lines: Name the beta blocker as succinate, carvedilol, or bisoprolol, not atenolol.
The reason each drug is on the list is one line, so the next clinician does not clean it up.
A low blood pressure that the patient tolerates is not an automatic stop.
miss: Stopping the ARNI at discharge because the ejection fraction is now 50%.

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: Improved ejection fraction remains on HFrEF therapy. Discharge instructions say not to stop the drugs.

title: Atrial fibrillation discharge is a rate and a stroke drug
lead: Discharge atrial fibrillation with a rate plan and an anticoagulant if the yearly risk is about 2% or higher. Rhythm control is not required for the prescription.
lines: Write the DOAC dose for the kidney function you measured.
Aspirin is not the stroke prescription.
A mechanical valve or severe mitral stenosis is warfarin, and the summary says so.
miss: Sending the patient out on aspirin because the rhythm converted in the emergency department.

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: Stroke prevention is prescribed from risk, with the dose adjusted to kidney function. Sinus rhythm does not cancel it.

title: New hypertension orders use two drugs when the pressure is 140/90 or higher
lead: For a confirmed pressure of 140/90 or higher, order two agents, preferably one pill, and a home-pressure follow-up.
lines: Use PREVENT if you are deciding on stage 1 treatment.
Do not use the 2017 pooled cohort equation in the note as if it were current.
A pregnancy test comes before an ACE inhibitor in a person who could be pregnant.
miss: Starting hydrochlorothiazide alone at 168/102 and saying come back in three months.

source.name: 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline.
source.says: Stage 2 hypertension starts two-drug therapy. Home readings and a pregnancy check before renin-angiotensin drugs are part of the order.

title: Dissection orders: beta blocker, surgeon, no lytic
lead: Order a beta blocker, a surgical consult, and pain control for a suspected ascending dissection. Write no thrombolysis on the chart.
lines: A pure vasodilator is not the first blood-pressure drug.
Type and screen and large-bore access are ordered.
The CT is expedited. It is not a routine add-on.
miss: Activating the stroke or STEMI lytic pathway because the pain is severe.

source.name: StatPearls. Aortic Dissection.
source.says: Heart-rate control, surgical consultation, and avoidance of thrombolysis are the orders for ascending dissection.

title: A rupturing aneurysm is blood bank and a surgeon
lead: Order a type and screen, large-bore access, and immediate surgical or endovascular consultation for a suspected rupture. Do not order a clinic ultrasound.
lines: Permissive hypotension is discussed. Do not bolus to a normal pressure before control.
A known aneurysm diameter in the chart is retrieved.
The family is updated because the patient may not be able to consent.
miss: Ordering a CT for the next available slot and a liter of crystalloid in a pressure of 80.

source.name: StatPearls. Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
source.says: Rupture orders are resuscitation without over-resuscitation, blood availability, and immediate repair.

title: Tamponade orders are fluids and drainage
lead: Order a fluid bolus as a bridge and pericardial drainage. Do not order furosemide.
lines: The echo is stat if the patient is not already crashing.
Reversal of anticoagulation is ordered if the effusion is bloody and the drug is on board.
A pericardial window is the plan if the fluid will reaccumulate.
miss: Ordering a diuretic for the elevated neck veins.

source.name: StatPearls. Cardiac Tamponade.
source.says: Fluids temporize and drainage treats. Diuretics are contraindicated.

title: Torsades orders: magnesium, potassium, and stop the QT drug
lead: Order intravenous magnesium, a potassium, and discontinuation of the QT-prolonging drug. Defibrillate if the patient is unstable.
lines: Do not order amiodarone for pause-dependent polymorphic tachycardia with a long QT.
The offending antibiotic or antiemetic is named on the allergy or avoid list.
A congenital long QT gets a specialist before discharge if the patient presented with syncope.
miss: Ordering amiodarone and continuing the azithromycin.

source.name: StatPearls. Long QT Syndrome.
source.says: Magnesium and potassium repletion are ordered, QT-prolonging drugs are stopped, and unstable patients are defibrillated.

title: Endocarditis orders: three cultures, then the drug if unstable
lead: Order three sets of blood cultures from separate sites. If the patient is unstable, the antibiotic follows the cultures immediately. If stable, wait for the draws.
lines: An echo is ordered. A transthoracic study may miss a small vegetation.
Dentist clearance is not today's order.
Hold anticoagulation decisions for a stroke until imaging says whether the infarct is hemorrhagic.
miss: Giving an oral antibiotic in the clinic and culturing the blood the next day.

source.name: StatPearls. Infective Endocarditis.
source.says: Multiple blood cultures precede antibiotics when the patient can wait a few minutes. Unstable patients are treated immediately afterward.

title: A tet spell order is knees, oxygen, and a vasoconstrictor if it continues
lead: Order calming, knee-chest position, oxygen, and a vasoconstrictor if the spell continues. Do not order a vasodilator.
lines: The murmur softening is recorded.
Morphine or a similar calming drug is part of some pathways. The point is the resistance.
The surgical team that knows this heart is called.
miss: Giving a drug that drops afterload during a spell.

source.name: StatPearls. Tetralogy of Fallot.
source.says: Knee-chest positioning, oxygen, and measures that raise systemic resistance are the orders. Vasodilators are avoided.

title: Coarctation follow-up is a leg pressure at every visit
lead: After coarctation repair, every visit includes a leg blood pressure and a question about headaches and exercise. Residual or recurrent narrowing is how these patients present as adults.
lines: A bicuspid valve is listened for.
Hypertension can persist after a good repair and is still treated to the adult goal.
Pregnancy is planned with a cardiologist.
miss: Treating an arm pressure of 150 and never checking the leg.

source.name: StatPearls. Coarctation of the Aorta.
source.says: Lifelong blood-pressure checks include the legs. Residual coarctation and a bicuspid valve remain part of adult care.

title: HFpEF admission is decongestion and the SGLT2 inhibitor
lead: Admit HFpEF for decongestion and continue or start an SGLT2 inhibitor. Do not build a HFrEF four-drug list the patient does not have an indication for.
lines: Blood pressure is treated to the current goal.
Atrial fibrillation rate is controlled because it steals filling time.
Daily weights are the discharge tool.
miss: Adding carvedilol, spironolactone, and an ARNI to every preserved-ejection-fraction admission.

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: Decongestion and an SGLT2 inhibitor are the HFpEF plan. The reduced-ejection-fraction regimen is not copied automatically.

title: Flutter discharge includes stroke prevention
lead: Discharge typical flutter with a rate or rhythm plan and the same stroke-prevention decision you would make for fibrillation.
lines: Isthmus ablation is the referral, written with a time.
Anticoagulation is not stopped because today's ECG is sinus.
The sawtooth is named in the summary so the next clinician does not call it sinus tachycardia.
miss: Stopping the DOAC after a flutter cardioversion.

source.name: StatPearls. Electrophysiology Study and Ablation of Atrial Flutter.
source.says: Stroke prevention follows risk and continues after cardioversion. Ablation is the rhythm referral for typical flutter.

title: Rheumatic prophylaxis is a scheduled penicillin, written for years
lead: Write the secondary-prevention penicillin as a scheduled drug with a duration, not as a one-time course.
lines: The valve findings are in the summary.
A new sore throat is still treated and is not a reason to stop prophylaxis.
Dental care is encouraged. Prophylaxis for dental work is a separate, narrower indication.
miss: Writing take until gone on a 10-day amoxicillin course and no further plan.

source.name: StatPearls. Rheumatic Heart Disease.
source.says: Secondary prophylaxis is scheduled and prolonged. It is not a single treatment course for pharyngitis.

title: A mechanical valve's warfarin is not swapped for a DOAC at discharge
lead: The discharge anticoagulant for a mechanical valve or for moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis is warfarin. Do not substitute a DOAC on the medication reconciliation.
lines: The INR target is the valve's target and is written as a number.
Aspirin may be added for some valves. It does not replace warfarin.
A DOAC on the home list of a mechanical valve is an error you correct.
miss: Reconciling apixaban onto a mechanical mitral valve because the patient prefers it.

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: Warfarin remains the anticoagulant for mechanical valves and moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis.

title: Unstable angina is admitted for serial ECGs
lead: Rest pain without a troponin rise is admitted or observed for serial ECGs. It is not a clinic appointment tomorrow.
lines: Aspirin is given if it is safe.
A repeat ECG is timed, not left to chance.
A truly stable, brief, exertional pain with a normal ECG is a different, faster outpatient path.
miss: Discharging rest pain because the first troponin was negative.

source.name: StatPearls. Unstable Angina.
source.says: Rest angina is observed with serial ECGs even when the first troponin is negative.

title: Dilated cardiomyopathy discharge names the alcohol stop
lead: If alcohol caused the dilated cardiomyopathy, the discharge order says stop drinking, in plain words, and continues the heart-failure drugs if the ejection fraction is low.
lines: The ejection fraction is on the summary so the drugs are not cleaned off.
A viral or chemotherapy cause is named if that is the history.
Follow-up imaging is dated.
miss: A diuretic prescription and no mention of alcohol.

source.name: StatPearls. Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
source.says: Alcohol cessation is an explicit discharge instruction when alcohol is the cause. Reduced ejection fraction stays on guideline-directed therapy.

title: Restrictive disease: order light chains before another diuretic increase
lead: A thick ventricle with low electrocardiographic voltage gets a light-chain order before you keep increasing the diuretic. Amyloid is the diagnosis you are missing.
lines: Diuresis still treats congestion. It is not the only order.
Digoxin is used cautiously if amyloid is likely, because the drug binds the amyloid.
The heart-failure clinic is not a substitute for the protein studies.
miss: A third increase in the loop diuretic and no protein studies.

source.name: StatPearls. Restrictive Cardiomyopathy.
source.says: Low voltage with a thick ventricle prompts a light-chain evaluation for amyloid. Diuresis does not replace that test.

title: Do not order endocarditis prophylaxis for an ordinary mitral valve prolapse
lead: An isolated mitral valve click does not get an endocarditis-prophylaxis order. Reserve prophylaxis for the short list of high-risk hearts.
lines: The click is documented so the next clinician does not call it a new murmur.
Severe regurgitation is followed. The click alone is not an operation.
A dental problem is treated by the dentist. A standing amoxicillin prescription is not the plan.
miss: Writing take 2 g of amoxicillin before every cleaning for a mid-systolic click.

source.name: StatPearls. Mitral Valve Prolapse.
source.says: Isolated mitral valve prolapse is not an indication for routine endocarditis prophylaxis.

title: COPD exacerbation orders: steroid, oxygen target, and selective antibiotics
lead: Order a short systemic steroid, titrated oxygen, and antibiotics only if sputum purulence comes with more dyspnea or volume. Order noninvasive ventilation if the pH is acid and the CO2 is high.
lines: Continue or start the long-acting inhalers before discharge.
A chest film looks for pneumonia and pneumothorax.
Follow-up is days, not a month, after a hospitalization.
miss: Ordering a 14-day antibiotic and high-flow oxygen for every wheeze.

source.name: GOLD 2026 Report. Key changes.
source.says: Steroids treat the exacerbation, antibiotics are selective, and noninvasive ventilation is for acute respiratory acidosis.

title: Asthma admission: oxygen only under 92, steroid if severe
lead: Order oxygen only if saturation is under 92, with a target at or under 95. Order a systemic steroid for a severe attack and the patient's ICS-formoterol plan at discharge.
lines: A nonrebreather is not the default.
Review the inhaler technique before discharge.
Anaphylaxis, if present, gets epinephrine first.
miss: Putting every asthma patient on 15 liters and discharging without a steroid inhaler.

source.name: 2026 GINA Strategy Report.
source.says: Oxygen is restricted to saturation below 92% with an upper target of 95%. Severe attacks receive a systemic corticosteroid, and the preventer is in place at discharge.

title: Pneumonia orders name the bed and the bug coverage separately
lead: Write the site of care from hypoxia, pressure, and confusion, then the antibiotic that matches that site. Do not add metronidazole by default.
lines: Severe disease is a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or a fluoroquinolone.
Blood cultures are ordered for severe disease.
A CURB-65 score is a note, not a substitute for looking at the patient.
miss: Admitting a comfortable patient with a normal saturation for intravenous antibiotics, or sending a hypoxic patient home.

source.name: 2019 IDSA/ATS Guideline for Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
source.says: Site of care is ordered from severity. Anaerobic coverage is not routine, and severe disease is combination therapy.

title: A stable embolus goes home or to the floor on a DOAC, not a lytic
lead: Order a DOAC for a stable pulmonary embolus if the bleeding risk allows it. Order a lytic only if the pressure is down or the patient is in shock.
lines: If the scan is delayed and suspicion is high, the anticoagulant is ordered now.
Right-heart strain is written in the note and does not by itself order the lytic.
Follow-up for provocation and cancer is named, not done as a full-body scan tonight.
miss: Ordering systemic thrombolysis because the CT said saddle.

source.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for Acute Pulmonary Embolism.
source.says: Stable patients are anticoagulated. Systemic thrombolysis is reserved for high-risk, hypotensive embolism.

title: SGLT2 inhibitor: hold tonight if the patient is not eating
lead: If the patient is fasting, going to surgery, or critically ill, hold the SGLT2 inhibitor tonight and write when to restart it. Do not discontinue it for a 4-point eGFR dip.
lines: Check ketones if the patient is nauseated and the glucose is not very high.
The indication, heart failure or kidney disease, is on the summary so it is restarted.
A sick-day plan is in the discharge instructions.
miss: Continuing the SGLT2 inhibitor through a nothing-by-mouth day and an operation.

source.name: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD.
source.says: The drug is held for prolonged fasting, surgery, and critical illness, and it is not stopped for the early hemodynamic eGFR dip.

title: Hyponatremia seizure: a bolus of 3% and a recheck
lead: Order a bolus of hypertonic saline for a seizure from hyponatremia and recheck the sodium immediately. Do not order a slow correction as the only order.
lines: The daily limit is still respected after the seizure stops.
Fluid restriction is the order for the stable SIADH patient, not for the seizing one.
The cause, a drug or a cancer, is on the problem list.
miss: Ordering fluid restriction and a sodium in the morning for a seizing patient.

source.name: StatPearls. Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion.
source.says: Severe symptoms are treated with a hypertonic bolus and an immediate recheck. Overcorrection is then avoided.

title: Diabetes insipidus orders: let them drink or replace the water
lead: Order free access to water or a matched intravenous replacement, and desmopressin only if the trial showed a central cause.
lines: A sodium is checked after each desmopressin dose.
Nephrogenic disease from lithium does not get escalating desmopressin.
The urine output is recorded hourly until it is stable.
miss: Restricting a hypernatremic patient to 1 liter a day.

source.name: StatPearls. Arginine Vasopressin Disorder (Diabetes Insipidus).
source.says: Water replacement is ordered. Desmopressin is reserved for central disease and is followed with sodium checks.

title: Tension pneumothorax: needle, then tube, no film first
lead: Order needle or finger decompression and a chest tube. Do not order a chest film as the first order in a crashing patient.
lines: Oxygen and large-bore access are ordered with it.
The side is written in the order so the wrong side is not opened.
A stable simple pneumothorax can have the film.
miss: Ordering a two-view chest radiograph stat on a patient with a pressure of 70 and a shifted trachea.

source.name: StatPearls. Tension Pneumothorax.
source.says: Decompression and a chest tube are the orders. Imaging waits until the patient is stable.

title: ARDS ventilator orders use height, not the scale
lead: Order tidal volume from predicted body weight using height and sex, about 6 mL per kilogram, and a plateau-pressure limit of 30.
lines: Write the height in the order so the next respiratory therapist does not use actual weight.
A high CO2 is tolerated.
Fluids are conservative once shock is resuscitated.
miss: Ordering 700 mL breaths because the patient weighs 120 kilograms.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
source.says: Tidal volume is calculated from predicted body weight. Plateau pressure is limited, and permissive hypercapnia is accepted.

title: Pulmonary fibrosis discharge is oxygen if hypoxic and an antifibrotic referral
lead: Discharge idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis with oxygen if the saturation requires it, pulmonary rehabilitation, and a referral for an antifibrotic. Do not discharge on a prednisone taper as the disease treatment.
lines: Vaccines are updated.
A new exposure or a connective-tissue symptom reopens the diagnosis.
Transplant referral is for the patient who is early enough to benefit.
miss: A 40-milligram prednisone taper as the only discharge drug.

source.name: StatPearls. Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
source.says: Oxygen, rehabilitation, and antifibrotic referral are the plan. Long-term prednisone is not disease-modifying therapy.

title: Bronchiectasis discharge teaches clearance
lead: Discharge bronchiectasis with a written airway-clearance plan and an antibiotic only for this flare. Name the follow-up that looks for the cause.
lines: Sputum culture is sent before the antibiotic if the patient can produce it.
A vest or a breathing technique is specified, not the word clearance.
Smoking cessation is ordered if it applies.
miss: A rotating antibiotic calendar and no clearance instruction.

source.name: StatPearls. Bronchiectasis.
source.says: Airway clearance is the discharge prescription. Antibiotics treat the current flare.

title: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis discharge names the antigen to remove
lead: The discharge instruction names the bird, the hot tub, or the barn to leave. A steroid prescription without that sentence is incomplete.
lines: Work exposure is a written restriction if that is the antigen.
Oxygen is ordered if the saturation requires it.
Follow-up imaging is timed.
miss: A steroid taper and a return to the same coop.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis.
source.says: Antigen removal is written into the discharge instructions. Steroids do not replace it.

title: Hyperkalemia with ECG changes: calcium first
lead: If the ECG shows peaked T waves or a wide QRS, order intravenous calcium first, then a shift, then a removal. A number without an ECG still gets a removal plan.
lines: Insulin and glucose shift potassium and can drop the glucose. Order a recheck.
Stop the spironolactone or the ACE inhibitor that caused it if the level is dangerous.
Dialysis is the order when the kidney cannot remove it and the level is severe.
miss: Ordering only kayexalate for a wide QRS.

source.name: StatPearls. Hyperkalemia.
source.says: Intravenous calcium stabilizes the membrane when the ECG is changing. Shift and removal follow. The cause is stopped.

title: Hypokalemia orders include magnesium and a route that is not a push
lead: Order magnesium with the potassium, and order the intravenous potassium as an infusion with a rate. A push is not an order you write.
lines: Oral is preferred when the ECG is quiet and the patient can swallow.
Recheck after the infusion.
The diuretic dose is changed on the same order.
miss: Writing potassium chloride 40 mEq IV push.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypokalemia.
source.says: Potassium is infused, never pushed, and magnesium is replaced so the potassium is retained.

title: Symptomatic hypocalcemia is calcium gluconate and a magnesium
lead: Order calcium gluconate for tetany, a seizure, or a long QT, and order a magnesium level with it.
lines: Recheck the calcium after the dose.
A post-thyroidectomy patient has the calcium ordered on a schedule, not after the first twitch.
Correct a low albumin before you treat a paper-low total calcium in a comfortable patient.
miss: A one-time oral calcium for a seizing post-operative patient.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypocalcemia.
source.says: Intravenous calcium is the order for severe symptoms. Magnesium is measured because deficiency prevents correction.

title: Respiratory acidosis: a ventilation order, not an oxygen order
lead: Order noninvasive ventilation or intubation for an acidemic, hypercapnic patient who is tiring. Do not order only a higher oxygen flow.
lines: A reversible sedative is stopped.
The chronic bicarbonate is respected so you do not overshoot.
A blood gas is timed after the ventilation starts.
miss: Turning the nasal cannula from 2 liters to 8 liters as the treatment of a pH of 7.15.

source.name: StatPearls. Respiratory Acidosis.
source.says: Ventilatory support is ordered for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure. Oxygen alone does not remove carbon dioxide.

title: Metabolic alkalosis: saline if the urine chloride is low
lead: Order saline and potassium when the urine chloride is low. Do not order saline for a high urine chloride from aldosterone.
lines: Stop the diuretic if it is still running and the patient is volume-down.
A chloride is on the chemistry, not assumed.
Acetazolamide is a selected order when volume cannot be given.
miss: A liter of saline for a hypertensive patient with a urine chloride of 40 and a renin that is suppressed.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Metabolic Alkalosis.
source.says: Saline is ordered for chloride-responsive alkalosis. Mineralocorticoid excess is not treated with saline.

title: Hypernatremia orders replace water on a schedule
lead: Order free-water replacement with a rate and a sodium check, not a single open bag. The drop is gradual.
lines: Desmopressin is added only for proven central diabetes insipidus.
The patient who can drink is allowed to.
A sodium is on the morning labs and sooner if the replacement is intravenous.
miss: An open order for D5W at 250 mL an hour with no recheck.

source.name: StatPearls. Hypernatremia.
source.says: Free water is replaced gradually with scheduled sodium checks to avoid cerebral edema.

title: Adult polycystic disease: image a sudden headache
lead: Order urgent brain imaging for a sudden severe headache in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. The blood pressure is treated at the same visit.
lines: Do not biopsy the kidney to confirm a diagnosis the family history and the ultrasound already made.
Tolvaptan, if used, comes with a liver-test plan.
A hematuria after minor trauma is rest and follow-up, not a cancer panic, unless it persists.
miss: Scheduling a routine clinic MRI of the brain for next month after a thunderclap headache.

source.name: StatPearls. Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
source.says: Sudden headache is imaged urgently because of aneurysm risk. Hypertension is treated. Biopsy is not the diagnostic test.

title: Uric acid colic: alkalinize and do not trust the plain film
lead: Order urine alkalinization and pain control for a uric acid stone. Do not discharge on the basis of a clear abdominal film.
lines: A CT or ultrasound is the image if you need to see it.
Allopurinol is not the acute pain drug.
Strain the urine and the follow-up is written.
miss: Telling the patient the stone is gone because the KUB is negative.

source.name: StatPearls. Uric Acid Nephrolithiasis.
source.says: Alkalinization and analgesia are the acute orders. Plain films do not exclude the stone.

title: Phosphate binders are timed with meals on the discharge list
lead: Write the phosphate binder with meals, in those words. A bedtime-only instruction does not bind phosphate.
lines: The dietitian order is part of the discharge.
Calcium and phosphate are both on the follow-up labs.
An SGLT2 inhibitor for the CKD indication is a separate line and is not the binder.
miss: Take one tablet at bedtime on the prescription.

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD).
source.says: Binders are prescribed with meals. Follow-up labs include calcium and phosphate.

title: Renal-artery stenosis: recheck creatinine after the ACE inhibitor
lead: If you start an ACE inhibitor in suspected bilateral renal-artery stenosis or a solitary kidney, order a creatinine within days. A young woman with fibromuscular disease is referred for revascularization rather than stented by habit.
lines: An older atherosclerotic stenosis is not automatically stented.
The blood pressure still needs treatment.
A bruit is documented and is not the whole diagnosis.
miss: Starting lisinopril and scheduling the next creatinine in six months.

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Artery Stenosis.
source.says: Creatinine is rechecked soon after renin-angiotensin blockade when the whole renal mass may sit behind a stenosis.

title: Emphysematous pyelonephritis is admitted for drainage
lead: Admit, order intravenous antibiotics, and consult urology or interventional radiology for drainage. Do not prescribe oral antibiotics and discharge.
lines: A glucose is controlled because the patient is usually diabetic.
Imaging is the CT that showed the gas, and it is not repeated for curiosity.
A simple pyelonephritis without gas can still go home if the patient can drink.
miss: A three-day ciprofloxacin prescription for gas in the kidney.

source.name: StatPearls. Emphysematous Pyelonephritis.
source.says: Intravenous antibiotics and source drainage are the admission orders.

title: Ulcer bleed orders: two lines, a type and screen, transfuse at 7
lead: Order two large-bore IVs, a type and screen, and a transfusion threshold of 7 if there is no active cardiovascular disease. Endoscopy is after resuscitation, within 24 hours.
lines: A proton-pump inhibitor infusion follows high-risk endoscopic stigmata.
Do not scope an unstable patient.
A higher threshold is written explicitly if the patient has active heart disease.
miss: Transfusing to a hemoglobin of 10 before the endoscopy.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Upper Gastrointestinal and Ulcer Bleeding.
source.says: Restrictive transfusion at 7 g/dL is the order without cardiovascular disease. Endoscopy follows resuscitation.

title: Variceal bleed orders: octreotide, an antibiotic, and a scope
lead: Order octreotide, an intravenous antibiotic, and urgent endoscopy. Do not order a beta blocker while the patient is in shock.
lines: Intubate before the scope if the hematemesis is massive.
Band ligation is the endoscopic plan.
The beta blocker is a discharge drug after the bleeding has stopped.
miss: Starting propranolol in the resuscitation bay.

source.name: StatPearls. Esophageal Varices.
source.says: Vasoactive therapy, antibiotics, and urgent banding are the orders. Beta blockade waits until hemostasis and a tolerable pressure.

title: New ascites: tap before you raise the diuretic
lead: Order a diagnostic tap before you increase the diuretic for new or worsened ascites. Send a cell count, albumin, and a bedside-inoculated culture.
lines: A neutrophil count of 250 or more is antibiotics now.
Albumin is ordered if you remove more than 5 liters.
A SAAG of 1.1 or more is portal hypertension and changes the differential.
miss: Doubling the spironolactone over the phone for a new tense abdomen.

source.name: StatPearls. Ascites.
source.says: Diagnostic paracentesis precedes a diuretic increase. Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis is treated when neutrophils are at least 250.

title: Pancreatitis orders: fluids and a diet when the pain allows
lead: Order lactated Ringer's or a similar crystalloid and a diet as soon as the pain allows. Do not order nothing by mouth for a week.
lines: Lipase does not need to be trended daily.
Antibiotics are not ordered for uncomplicated pancreatitis.
A rising urea or hematocrit is a reason to give more fluid, written as a reassessment.
miss: A week of bowel rest and prophylactic imipenem.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Pancreatitis.
source.says: Early oral feeding replaces prolonged fasting. Antibiotics are not routine for uncomplicated disease.

title: Jaundice means the stone may have left the gallbladder
lead: Cholecystitis with jaundice is not a simple gallbladder. Order an evaluation of the duct before you treat it as an isolated cystic-duct stone.
lines: Fever and low pressure with jaundice are a duct emergency, and antibiotics start while that evaluation is arranged.
Ultrasound of the gallbladder alone can miss the duct stone.
The gallbladder operation is still needed later. It is not the emergency drainage of a blocked duct.
miss: Booking an elective cholecystectomy next month for a jaundiced, febrile patient.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Cholecystitis.
source.says: Jaundice moves the problem beyond the cystic duct. The bile duct has to be evaluated, and infection is treated while that happens.

title: Cholecystitis: surgery consult and antibiotics, not antibiotics alone
lead: Order a surgical consult for early cholecystectomy and antibiotics. Do not discharge a febrile, Murphy-positive patient on oral antibiotics as the definitive plan.
lines: Pain control and nothing by mouth until surgery is the immediate order.
Ultrasound is the image if it has not been done.
Jaundice and hypotension move the diagnosis toward the duct and a different procedure.
miss: A 7-day antibiotic prescription and a clinic appointment for biliary colic that is actually cholecystitis.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Cholecystitis.
source.says: Early cholecystectomy is the definitive order. Antibiotics are adjunctive.

title: Bowel obstruction: suction, fluids, and a surgery call if ischemic
lead: Order nasogastric suction and fluids for a stable obstruction. Order an immediate surgical consult if there is fever, peritonitis, or a rising lactate.
lines: Prior surgery makes adhesions likely and does not make ischemia impossible.
A closed loop is named on the CT so it is not observed.
Antiemetics are given. Opioids are not the only plan.
miss: Observing a peritonitic obstruction overnight because the last one resolved.

source.name: StatPearls. Small Bowel Obstruction.
source.says: Suction and fluids are the stable-patient orders. Peritonitis, fever, or rising lactate trigger immediate surgery.

title: Mesenteric ischemia: CTA and a surgeon, lactate is not the gate
lead: Order CT angiography and a surgical consult when the pain is out of proportion. Do not wait for the lactate to rise.
lines: Heparin is ordered if an embolus is the working diagnosis and bleeding is not the problem.
A normal abdominal exam is written down so nobody is reassured by it.
Fluids and a lactate are ordered, and the lactate is not the permission to call.
miss: A lactate in the morning and a surgery consult if it is high.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Mesenteric Ischemia.
source.says: CT angiography and surgical consultation are immediate. A normal lactate does not delay them.

title: Do not start a gluten-free diet the week of the biopsy
lead: If you are confirming celiac disease with a biopsy, order the patient to keep eating gluten until the biopsy. A diet started early makes the test false.
lines: Check total IgA on the lab order.
Iron is replaced if the patient is deficient, and the cause is still proved.
The diet is the treatment after the test, and the referral to a dietitian is written.
miss: Congratulating a patient for two weeks of gluten avoidance before the endoscopy.

source.name: StatPearls. Celiac Disease.
source.says: Gluten is continued until serology and biopsy are complete. Total IgA is ordered with the antibody.

title: Severe colitis orders: admit, steroid, stop loperamide
lead: Admit severe ulcerative colitis, order a steroid, and discontinue loperamide and opioids. Order a stool study for C. difficile.
lines: A daily abdominal film is the order if the belly is distended.
Surgery is called early for a toxic megacolon.
The home mesalamine is not the treatment of this severity.
miss: Discharging on loperamide for ten bloody stools a day.

source.name: StatPearls. Ulcerative Colitis.
source.says: Severe disease is admitted for corticosteroids. Antimotility drugs are stopped, and infection is excluded.

title: Achalasia: nothing by mouth if aspirating, and a myotomy referral
lead: If the patient is aspirating, order nothing by mouth and a myotomy or dilation referral. Do not refill the proton-pump inhibitor as the treatment.
lines: Manometry is the outpatient confirmatory test if it has not been done.
Endoscopy is ordered to exclude a cancer mimic.
Aspiration precautions are written for tonight.
miss: A higher-dose proton-pump inhibitor and a regular diet.

source.name: StatPearls. Achalasia.
source.says: Aspiration risk leads to bowel rest and a definitive LES procedure. Acid suppression is not the treatment.

title: Chronic pancreatitis enzymes are written with meals
lead: Write the enzyme with each meal and snack. Order alcohol cessation as a prescription-level instruction, not a suggestion in the last line.
lines: A glucose is on the discharge labs.
A new jaundice is an imaging order before discharge.
Pain control is a plan that is not only opioids.
miss: One capsule at bedtime on the label.

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Pancreatitis.
source.says: Enzymes are timed to meals. Alcohol cessation and evaluation of new jaundice are part of the order.

title: H. pylori treatment is a regimen and a test of cure
lead: Order a full eradication regimen and a test of cure. Do not order a proton-pump inhibitor alone for a positive test.
lines: Stop the NSAID if it caused the ulcer.
The test of cure is timed after the antibiotics and after acid suppression is held.
Alarm symptoms still get an endoscopy rather than another empiric course.
miss: A proton-pump inhibitor refill and no test of cure.

source.name: StatPearls. Peptic Ulcer Disease.
source.says: Eradication therapy is prescribed and cure is confirmed. Acid suppression alone does not treat the infection.

title: DKA orders: potassium, then insulin, then dextrose
lead: Order a potassium before the insulin. If it is under 3.3, replace it first. Add dextrose when the glucose falls and keep the insulin running until the gap closes.
lines: Fluids are the first line of the order set.
Bicarbonate is not a routine order.
The home SGLT2 inhibitor is held and a sick-day plan is written.
miss: Stopping the insulin drip at a glucose of 180 with a bicarbonate of 8.

source.name: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report.
source.says: Potassium is known before insulin. Insulin continues, with dextrose, until ketoacidosis resolves.

title: Thyroid storm orders name the sequence
lead: Order a beta blocker and a thionamide, and write iodine after the thionamide has been given. Order a glucocorticoid and treat the trigger.
lines: Do not order aspirin for the fever.
The iodine order has a start time, not a simultaneous start.
Cooling and monitoring are part of the set.
miss: A single order for potassium iodide with no thionamide.

source.name: StatPearls. Thyroid Storm.
source.says: The order sequence is beta blockade and a thionamide, then iodine, plus a glucocorticoid.

title: Adrenal crisis: hydrocortisone and saline are stat
lead: Order hydrocortisone and normal saline as stat medications. Do not order a cosyntropin test as the first action.
lines: A glucose is on the labs because it may be low.
The home steroid is written as a stress dose, not the maintenance dose.
Antibiotics are added if sepsis is the trigger.
miss: A morning cortisol for tomorrow and a maintenance prednisone dose tonight.

source.name: StatPearls. Adrenal Insufficiency.
source.says: Stress-dose hydrocortisone and saline are immediate orders. Diagnostic stimulation testing waits.

title: Pheochromocytoma preparation is an alpha blocker on the list before surgery
lead: The preoperative orders show an alpha blocker already in place and volume restored. A beta blocker is not the first preoperative drug.
lines: Metanephrines are resulted before the incision, not drawn in the operating room.
The anesthesia team is told.
A hypertensive crisis order, phentolamine or a similar alpha drug, is available.
miss: A preoperative beta blocker and an empty alpha-blocker line.

source.name: StatPearls. Pheochromocytoma.
source.says: Alpha blockade and volume replacement are completed before surgery. Beta blockade is not first.

title: Pregnancy hypertension at 140/90 is a treatment order
lead: For chronic hypertension in pregnancy, order treatment at 140/90 rather than waiting for 160/110. ACE inhibitors and ARBs are not on the list.
lines: Labetalol or nifedipine is the usual agent.
Home pressures are ordered, not a single clinic number.
Aspirin prevention is a different order and does not treat today's severe pressure.
miss: Continuing lisinopril and observing until the pressure is severe.

source.name: ACOG Practice Advisory. Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP).
source.says: Treatment starts at 140/90. ACE inhibitors and ARBs are stopped. Severe-range pressures are a separate emergency.

title: Severe pregnancy hypertension is treated within the hour
lead: Order an intravenous or immediate-release oral antihypertensive for a sustained pressure of 160 or 110, and order magnesium for seizure prevention. Do not wait for labs.
lines: Recheck the pressure on a schedule after the dose.
The goal is not a normal pressure of 110. Overcorrection harms the placenta.
Postpartum patients get the same order. Discharge does not end the risk.
miss: Waiting for the preeclampsia labs before the first dose of labetalol.

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia.
source.says: Severe-range pressures are treated promptly. Magnesium is ordered for seizure prophylaxis and does not replace the antihypertensive.

title: Aspirin for preeclampsia is ordered after 12 weeks in high-risk patients
lead: Order 81 mg of aspirin after 12 weeks for a high-risk patient, and do not order it as the treatment of a pressure that is already severe.
lines: The high-risk list is prior preeclampsia, multiples, chronic hypertension, diabetes, kidney disease, or autoimmune disease.
Start it at the visit you identify the risk, not at 34 weeks.
The severe-pressure order is a different drug.
miss: Starting aspirin at the delivery admission for a pressure of 180.

source.name: USPSTF. Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia.
source.says: Low-dose aspirin after 12 weeks is a prevention order for high-risk patients.

title: Ectopic: surgery if unstable, methotrexate only if every criterion is met
lead: Order the operating room for an unstable ectopic pregnancy. Order methotrexate only if the patient is stable, the hCG is in range, and follow-up is certain.
lines: A type and screen is on the unstable patient's orders.
Rh immunoglobulin is ordered if the patient is Rh negative.
A discharge on methotrexate includes the day of the next hCG.
miss: Methotrexate and a discharge for a dizzy patient with a positive pregnancy test.

source.name: StatPearls. Ectopic Pregnancy.
source.says: Unstable patients go to surgery. Methotrexate discharges include verified follow-up and selection criteria.

title: Abruption orders are blood and a fetal monitor
lead: Order blood products, a fetal monitor, and large-bore access. Do not order a digital cervical exam.
lines: A fibrinogen is on the labs.
The obstetric team is called when the diagnosis is suspected.
Pain control is ordered and does not delay resuscitation.
miss: A cervical check as the first order.

source.name: StatPearls. Placental Abruption.
source.says: Resuscitation, coagulation studies, and fetal monitoring are the orders. Digital examination waits until previa is excluded.

title: Previa orders: no digital exam, ultrasound, and a cesarean plan
lead: Order pelvic rest, an ultrasound, and a cesarean plan if the placenta covers the cervix. Write no digital exam.
lines: A prior cesarean plus previa triggers an accreta plan at a capable hospital.
The acute bleed gets the same blood-bank orders as any maternal hemorrhage.
An outpatient bleed that has stopped still leaves with precautions and a dated delivery plan.
miss: An induction order for a complete previa.

source.name: StatPearls. Placenta Previa.
source.says: No digital examination is written as an order. Complete previa is a cesarean plan, and accreta risk changes the location.

title: Gestational diabetes discharge watches the newborn and rescreens the mother
lead: Order an early feed and a glucose check for the newborn, and a postpartum diabetes test for the mother. Insulin, if used, is not automatically continued at the pregnancy dose.
lines: The mother is taught the sick-day difference between pregnancy and afterward.
A very high postpartum glucose is treated, not ignored because the pregnancy ended.
Contraception is discussed because the next pregnancy's glucose starts before the first prenatal visit.
miss: Discharging the pair with no neonatal glucose and no maternal follow-up test.

source.name: StatPearls. Gestational Diabetes.
source.says: Neonatal glucose is checked and the mother is rescreened for diabetes after delivery.

title: Ask about PDE-5 inhibitors before the first nitroglycerin
lead: The chest-pain order set includes a question about PDE-5 inhibitors before nitroglycerin is given. If the answer is yes, the nitrate is not given.
lines: The ECG and aspirin are still ordered.
Document the time of the last dose if you know it.
Do not guess that enough hours have passed if you are unsure.
miss: Giving the nitrate because the protocol says so.

source.name: StatPearls. Erectile Dysfunction.
source.says: Nitroglycerin is withheld after a recent PDE-5 inhibitor. The rest of the ACS evaluation proceeds.

title: BPH retention is a catheter, not a sample of tamsulosin
lead: Acute urinary retention gets a catheter and a recorded residual. An alpha blocker is started after the bladder is empty, not instead of emptying it.
lines: A creatinine is ordered if retention was prolonged.
A nodule is not attributed to hyperplasia.
Finasteride is not the drug that empties the bladder tonight.
miss: A tamsulosin prescription and no catheter for a painful full bladder.

source.name: StatPearls. Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
source.says: Retention is drained. An alpha blocker may be started afterward. A 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor does not relieve acute retention.

title: Testicular torsion: consent for the operating room, not a morning ultrasound
