lead: Write the surgical consent and the nothing-by-mouth order when the exam is torsion. Ultrasound is ordered only if it will not consume the window and the exam is unclear.
lines: The contralateral orchiopexy is part of the consent.
Pain medicine is ordered and does not delay the room.
A urology call is a now call.
miss: An ultrasound order for 8 a.m. and a regular diet.

source.name: StatPearls. Testicular Torsion.
source.says: Operative exploration is ordered immediately for a convincing exam. Imaging is not allowed to delay it.

title: Ovarian torsion: surgical consent even when Doppler shows flow
lead: Order surgical evaluation for suspected ovarian torsion regardless of a Doppler report that shows flow. Order a pregnancy test.
lines: Nothing by mouth and consent are written.
Pain control is ordered.
An ectopic pregnancy remains on the differential until the test returns.
miss: Cancelling the surgical consult because the report said flow was present.

source.name: StatPearls. Ovarian Torsion.
source.says: Operative evaluation is ordered on clinical grounds. Doppler flow is not a cancellation criterion.

title: Pelvic inflammatory disease: treat the partner in the note
lead: The discharge names the partner treatment and the return precautions for worsening pain. A pregnancy test is resulted before the drug.
lines: An abscess that is not improving gets a drainage order, not another day of the same antibiotic only.
Perihepatitis is not discharged as simple biliary colic.
Follow-up testing for cure or reinfection is written.
miss: A prescription with no mention of the partner and no return precautions.

source.name: StatPearls. Pelvic Inflammatory Disease.
source.says: Partner treatment and follow-up are part of the order. Abscesses that fail antibiotics are drained.

title: Postmenopausal bleeding is a biopsy order, not a repeat Pap
lead: Order an endometrial biopsy or a referral that will do one. Do not order a repeat Pap smear as the evaluation.
lines: Ultrasound stripe thickness can triage some patients and does not replace a biopsy when bleeding is persistent.
Stop unopposed estrogen if that is the cause, and still evaluate.
Anticoagulation is not an adequate explanation by itself.
miss: A repeat Pap smear in a year.

source.name: StatPearls. Endometrial Cancer.
source.says: Endometrial sampling is the order. Cervical cytology does not evaluate the endometrium.

title: Hyperthyroidism in pregnancy: the drug matches the trimester
lead: Order propylthiouracil in the first trimester and a plan to change to methimazole afterward. Do not order radioactive iodine.
lines: The lowest controlling dose is written, with a thyroid test interval.
Both drugs cross the placenta.
Uncontrolled disease is more dangerous than the drug, so do not stop treatment entirely.
miss: Continuing methimazole from conception through week 10, or ordering a thyroid scan.

source.name: StatPearls. Hyperthyroidism in Pregnancy.
source.says: Propylthiouracil is used in the first trimester. Radioactive iodine is contraindicated. The dose is the lowest that controls the mother.

title: A pituitary mass with a TSH of 80 is thyroid hormone, not a surgical date
lead: Order thyroid hormone and a repeat image for pituitary enlargement caused by severe hypothyroidism. Do not book surgery first.
lines: A prolactin is interpreted in light of the TSH.
The surgical referral is cancelled or delayed until the thyroid is replaced.
The patient is warned that the mass can shrink.
miss: A transsphenoidal date for a patient whose TSH has not been checked.

source.name: StatPearls. Pituitary Hyperplasia in Primary Hypothyroidism.
source.says: Thyroid replacement is the order. Surgery is deferred until hyperplasia has had time to regress.

title: Sepsis orders are lactate, cultures, drug, and a fluid with a reassessment
lead: Order a lactate, cultures if they will not delay the drug, a broad antibiotic, and crystalloid if the pressure is low or the lactate is at least 4. Order a blood pressure reassessment, not an unmeasured bolus.
lines: A vasopressor is ordered if the pressure stays low, aimed at a mean pressure of 65.
The suspected source is named so the drug matches it.
A virus swab does not replace the antibiotic.
miss: One liter of fluid and a lactate in the morning.

source.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 Adult Guidelines.
source.says: The hour-1 actions are lactate, cultures, antibiotics, crystalloid for hypoperfusion, and vasopressors if hypotension persists.

title: Anaphylaxis: epinephrine in the thigh, and a period of watching
lead: Order intramuscular epinephrine in the mid-outer thigh and a period of observation. Do not order diphenhydramine as the only drug.
lines: The adult dose is 0.3 to 0.5 mg of the 1 mg/mL concentration.
A second dose is ordered if the first fails.
The patient does not drive home ten minutes later.
miss: Diphenhydramine, a steroid, and discharge in ten minutes.

source.name: StatPearls. Anaphylaxis.
source.says: Intramuscular epinephrine and observation are the orders. Antihistamines do not replace epinephrine.

title: Carbon monoxide: 100% oxygen now, and the cohabitants
lead: Order 100% oxygen and a carboxyhemoglobin. Ask who else was in the house and order them evaluated if they share the exposure.
lines: Do not be reassured by a pulse oximeter.
Hyperbaric oxygen is ordered for coma, pregnancy, or cardiac ischemia.
The source, a heater or a fire, is removed.
miss: Discharge on a normal pulse oximeter after a heater exposure.

source.name: StatPearls. Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.
source.says: High-flow oxygen is started immediately and co-exposed people are identified. Oximetry does not clear the patient.

title: Acetaminophen: start the antidote and plot the time
lead: Order N-acetylcysteine when the level is toxic or the time of a large ingestion is unknown. Write the time of ingestion on the order so the nomogram is used correctly.
lines: A staggered ingestion is not plotted on the single-time nomogram.
Charcoal is ordered only if the airway is safe and the ingestion was recent.
The ALT is trended. A normal first ALT is not a stop order.
miss: Holding the antidote for tomorrow's liver enzymes.

source.name: StatPearls. Acetaminophen Toxicity.
source.says: N-acetylcysteine is ordered for toxic and unplottable ingestions. The first enzyme does not clear the patient.

title: Naloxone is an order with a recheck, not a single dose and a goodbye
lead: Order naloxone and an observation period long enough for the opioid you suspect. A long-acting opioid gets a longer watch or an infusion.
lines: The airway is opened if the patient is apneic.
A second dose is written as a nursing parameter, not discovered when the patient stops breathing in the lobby.
The discharge names the risk of recurrence.
miss: One dose and a discharge at 20 minutes after methadone.

source.name: StatPearls. Opioid Toxicity.
source.says: Observation matches the opioid's duration. Recurrence of apnea is an expected order, not a surprise.

title: Do not order flumazenil on a daily benzodiazepine user
lead: Order airway support. Do not order flumazenil for a patient who takes a benzodiazepine every day.
lines: If an opioid is also on board, naloxone is the apnea drug.
A seizure from flumazenil is harder to treat if you just blocked the benzodiazepine.
A taper, not an antidote, is the discharge for dependence.
miss: Flumazenil intravenous once to facilitate discharge.

source.name: StatPearls. Benzodiazepine Toxicity.
source.says: Supportive care is ordered. Flumazenil is not ordered in dependent patients.

title: Alcohol withdrawal: a scored benzodiazepine protocol and thiamine first
lead: Order a symptom-triggered benzodiazepine protocol and thiamine before any glucose. Do not order haloperidol as the only withdrawal drug.
lines: A monitored bed is ordered for delirium tremens.
The last drink time is written so the team expects the late delirium.
Electrolytes, especially magnesium, are on the labs.
miss: Haloperidol every six hours and a glucose infusion with no thiamine.

source.name: StatPearls. Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome.
source.says: Symptom-triggered benzodiazepines and thiamine before glucose are the orders. Antipsychotics are not the withdrawal treatment.

title: Rhabdomyolysis: a fluid rate and a repeat potassium
lead: Order intravenous fluids at a stated rate and a repeat potassium. Order a microscope look at the urine, not only the dipstick.
lines: A compartment pressure or a surgical consult is ordered for a tight limb.
The statin is held on the order.
The creatine kinase is trended, not used as a one-time curiosity.
miss: A single bag of saline and no repeat potassium.

source.name: StatPearls. Rhabdomyolysis.
source.says: A defined fluid rate and repeat potassium are the orders. The urine is examined microscopically.

title: Malignant hyperthermia: stop the gas and give dantrolene
lead: The intraoperative order is to stop the volatile agent, hyperventilate with 100% oxygen, and give dantrolene. Cooling is ordered with it.
lines: The dantrolene dose is repeated as the protocol says. One vial is not the whole treatment.
Potassium and urine output are ordered because muscle is dying.
The team is told this is not light anesthesia.
miss: Increasing the vaporizer and ordering acetaminophen.

source.name: StatPearls. Malignant Hyperthermia.
source.says: The triggering anesthetic is stopped and dantrolene is given, with hyperventilation and cooling.

title: Fat embolism: oxygen and fix the fracture
lead: Order oxygen and early fracture fixation. Do not order heparin as the specific treatment of fat embolism.
lines: A chest finding and petechiae are documented.
A true venous clot is still considered and is a separate order.
The orthopedic team is called for the fixation, which is the source control.
miss: A heparin drip as the only order and a delayed fixation.

source.name: StatPearls. Fat Embolism and Fat Embolism Syndrome.
source.says: Supportive oxygen and fracture fixation are the orders. Heparin is not a specific fat-embolism antidote.

title: Delirium: stop diphenhydramine and search the bladder
lead: Order a stop to anticholinergic drugs, a bladder scan, and a search for infection. Do not order a benzodiazepine for a non-withdrawal delirium.
lines: Glasses and hearing aids are an order, not a courtesy.
Restraints are not the first safety order.
The family is asked what the patient was like last week.
miss: Lorazepam around the clock and a Foley catheter for convenience.

source.name: StatPearls. Differentiating Delirium Versus Dementia in Older Adults.
source.says: Deliriogenic drugs are stopped and reversible causes are sought. Benzodiazepines are not routine treatment.

title: A Beers list drug is removed at discharge if it caused the admission
lead: If a benzodiazepine, a strong anticholinergic, or sliding-scale insulin alone contributed to the admission, take it off the discharge list.
lines: The 2023 AGS Beers Criteria name the drugs to avoid in older adults.
Replace the indication, do not leave a hole: pain, sleep, or glucose still need a plan.
Tell the patient why the familiar pill is gone.
miss: Restarting the admission-causing benzodiazepine because it is on the home list.

source.name: 2023 AGS Beers Criteria.
source.says: Drugs that are potentially inappropriate and that contributed to harm are not restarted at discharge.

title: Opioid start: immediate release, a low dose, and naloxone if the risk is high
lead: If an opioid is started, order immediate release, the lowest effective dose, and naloxone if the patient has overdose risk. Do not start an extended-release opioid.
lines: A nonopioid is ordered for many acute pains and is not skipped.
The duration is days, written as a number.
Benzodiazepines are not combined without a reason you would defend.
miss: A long-acting opioid as the first prescription after an injury.

source.name: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids.
source.says: Initial opioids are immediate-release and low dose. Naloxone is offered when overdose risk is present. Extended-release opioids are not started first.

title: A handoff uses I-PASS out loud
lead: The handoff order of information is illness severity, a patient summary, the action list, situational awareness, and a synthesis by the receiver.
lines: The receiver says the plan back.
Illness severity is one word the next clinician can use at 3 a.m.
A written note that was not spoken is not a handoff.
miss: A signed-out list with no severity and no read-back.

source.name: Starmer et al. I-PASS. New England Journal of Medicine.
source.says: I-PASS structures the handoff: illness severity, patient summary, action list, situation awareness, and synthesis by the receiver.

title: A positive stool test orders a colonoscopy
lead: A positive stool-based colorectal test is followed by colonoscopy. Do not order a repeat stool test.
lines: The patient is told that before the first stool kit.
Average-risk screening still starts at 45.
Iron deficiency is a diagnostic colonoscopy, not a screening interval.
miss: Repeating the stool card after a positive result.

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal cancer screening.
source.says: A positive stool test is an indication for colonoscopy, not for another stool test.

title: A breast lump is a diagnostic order, not the next screening date
lead: A palpable breast mass is a diagnostic imaging order now. It is not postponed until the next biennial mammogram.
lines: Screening mammography is for people without that symptom.
Age 40 to 74 is the screening window. A mass at any age in that window is still diagnostic.
A family history suggestive of a BRCA-associated cancer is a different, earlier plan.
miss: Scheduling a screening mammogram in eight months for a new lump.

source.name: USPSTF. Breast cancer screening.
source.says: Screening schedules do not apply to a palpable mass. Diagnostic imaging is ordered.

title: Document the lung-screening conversation before the scan
lead: Before the first low-dose CT, document the shared decision: the benefit, the false positives, and that the patient still smokes or quit within 15 years.
lines: Eligibility is age 50 to 80 and at least 20 pack-years.
A symptomatic cough is a diagnostic CT, not a screening code.
The annual order stops when the patient is no longer eligible.
miss: Ordering the scan with no note that the patient agreed after hearing the harms.

source.name: USPSTF. Lung cancer screening.
source.says: Shared decision-making is documented before the initial low-dose CT. Symptoms convert the order from screening to diagnosis.

title: Stop cervical screening at 65 only if the prior tests were adequate
lead: You may stop cervical screening at 65 only when the recent tests were adequate and negative. A patient with no records is not stopped.
lines: HPV testing alone is not the order before age 30.
Bleeding after sex is examined now even if the last test was normal.
Vaccination does not delete the schedule.
miss: Stopping screening at 65 because the patient cannot remember her last Pap.

source.name: USPSTF. Cervical cancer screening.
source.says: Stopping at 65 requires adequate prior negative screening. Symptoms are evaluated regardless of the schedule.

title: Do not order HPV testing alone before age 30
lead: Ages 21 to 29 are cytology every 3 years. Do not order high-risk HPV testing alone in that age band.
lines: After 30, HPV testing every 5 years is an option.
A yearly Pap is not the recommendation.
A visible cervical lesion is a biopsy, not a screening interval.
miss: An HPV-only order for a 24-year-old.

source.name: USPSTF. Cervical cancer screening.
source.says: Primary HPV testing is not the strategy before age 30. Cytology every 3 years is.

title: Age 75 mammography is a decision, not an automatic order
lead: At 75 and older, do not order mammography automatically. The USPSTF found the evidence insufficient, so you decide with the patient.
lines: A lump is still diagnostic at any age.
A patient who would not treat a cancer found on the scan should not have the scan.
The every-other-year order applies through 74.
miss: A standing yearly mammogram order with no stop date for an 82-year-old.

source.name: USPSTF. Breast cancer screening.
source.says: Evidence is insufficient at age 75 and older, so screening is an individual decision rather than an automatic order.

title: Colon screening after 75 is selective
lead: From 76 to 85, colorectal screening is selective. It is not ordered for a patient whose other illnesses will not allow a benefit.
lines: Through 75 it is recommended for average risk.
A prior colonoscopy date is retrieved before you order another.
A positive prior stool test that was never scoped is completed.
miss: Ordering a first colonoscopy at 84 for a patient in hospice-level heart failure.

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal cancer screening.
source.says: Ages 76 to 85 are a selective offer based on health and prior screening, not an automatic start.

title: An early colon cancer in the family moves the start age
lead: A first-degree relative with colorectal cancer before 60, or two relatives at any age, starts screening earlier than 45. Order that earlier plan.
lines: Average risk remains 45.
The tool, often colonoscopy, is named.
Do not apply the average-risk stool-kit interval to a high-risk family.
miss: A stool kit at 45 for a patient whose father had colon cancer at 48.

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal cancer screening.
source.says: Family history of early colorectal cancer changes the start age and often the test. The average-risk age of 45 does not apply.

title: Do not order supplemental ultrasound for dense breasts as a proven add-on
lead: The USPSTF does not recommend supplemental ultrasound or MRI for dense breasts on an otherwise negative mammogram. Do not order it as if it were required.
lines: Density is discussed. It is not an automatic second test.
A lump is still imaged diagnostically.
The biennial mammogram remains the screening order.
miss: An automatic breast ultrasound every year because the report said dense.

source.name: USPSTF. Breast cancer screening.
source.says: Supplemental screening for dense breasts has an insufficient evidence grade and is not an automatic order.

title: A depression screen without a follow-up slot is an incomplete order
lead: If you screen for depression, the order includes a way to diagnose and treat this week. A form in the chart with no visit is not the USPSTF recommendation.
lines: Pregnancy and the postpartum months are included.
A positive score is an interview, not a prescription by itself.
A universal suicide questionnaire is not the required screen.
miss: A PHQ-9 in the portal with no one assigned to read it.

source.name: USPSTF. Screening for Depression in Adults.
source.says: Screening is recommended only when systems exist to diagnose and treat. An unread form does not meet that standard.

title: Do not build a quality metric out of a universal suicide screen
lead: Do not order a stand-alone suicide-risk questionnaire on every adult as a population screen. The USPSTF grade is I.
lines: Ask about suicide when the patient or the depression interview opens that door.
That question is care. It is not the same as a required screen.
A positive depression screen still gets an interview.
miss: A required suicide score on every annual visit with no depression question.

source.name: USPSTF. Suicide risk in adults and older adults.
source.says: The task force found insufficient evidence for stand-alone suicide-risk screening in all adults.

title: Write the absolute numbers in the after-visit summary
lead: When you recommend a preventive drug or a screen, the after-visit summary states the absolute benefit, not only a relative percentage.
lines: A 50% relative reduction of a rare event can be one in a thousand.
The harm, including false positives, is in the same sentence.
A patient who would decline the next step is not screened.
miss: A handout that says cuts your risk in half and gives no baseline.

source.name: USPSTF. Lung cancer screening.
source.says: Shared decision-making uses absolute benefits and harms. Relative reductions alone are misleading.

title: Do not order a screening test the patient would not act on
lead: If a patient would not accept a biopsy or a treatment for the disease you might find, do not order the screening test.
lines: Ask before the scan.
A diagnostic test for a symptom is different. Symptoms are still evaluated.
Document the refusal of screening, not a failure to offer it.
miss: Ordering a screening colonoscopy for a patient who has said they would never treat a cancer.

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal cancer screening.
source.says: Screening is offered to patients who could benefit from the downstream care. It is not ordered when that care would be declined.

title: Two positive-required tests will miss more people
lead: If you order two tests and require both to be positive before you act, tell the patient you will miss more disease. That structure raises specificity.
lines: Either-positive testing does the opposite.
Write which structure you intended so the next clinician does not mix them.
A single very sensitive test is a different order.
miss: Requiring both a sensitive and a specific test to be positive and thinking you lost no cases.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Series testing increases specificity and decreases sensitivity. The patient is told which misses become more likely.

title: Either-positive tests need a false-alarm plan
lead: If either of two tests being positive will trigger a biopsy, order the biopsy capacity before you order the pair. Parallel testing creates more false alarms.
lines: The patient is told that more alarms are the price of fewer misses.
Do not add the second test without a plan for the positive.
A pretest probability still comes first.
miss: Ordering every available test and a promise that a positive means the disease.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Parallel testing raises sensitivity and lowers specificity. The downstream plan for false positives is arranged first.

title: A lower cutoff is an order you defend
lead: If you lower a test's cutoff to miss fewer cases, write why, because you will label more healthy people as sick.
lines: You cannot have both perfect sensitivity and perfect specificity at one number.
The lab's reference range is the default unless you document a reason.
A cutoff copied from another population is not automatically yours.
miss: Lowering a cutoff and telling patients the test became more accurate in every way.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: A lower threshold increases sensitivity and decreases specificity. The trade is a deliberate order.

title: Do not quote a predictive value from a different population
lead: The positive predictive value you read in a paper does not transfer to your clinic if the disease is rarer here. Recalculate or do not quote it.
lines: Sensitivity can transfer. The predictive value cannot, without the local prevalence.
A screening fair and an emergency department do not share a predictive value.
Write the prevalence you assumed.
miss: Telling a low-risk patient the positive predictive value from a specialty-clinic study.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Predictive values depend on prevalence. A published predictive value is not cited as if it were universal.

title: Write the pre-test chance before you order a rare-disease test
lead: Before you order a test for a rare disease, write the chance you believe the patient has it. A positive result will often be false if that chance is tiny.
lines: Sensitivity does not rescue a near-zero pre-test chance.
The likelihood ratio then revises the number you wrote.
If you cannot name a pre-test chance, you are not ready to interpret the result.
miss: Ordering a rare-disease panel because it is on the menu, with no estimate of the chance.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Pre-test probability is recorded before a low-prevalence test. Positive results in that setting are often false.

title: The handoff note names severity in one line
lead: The written handoff starts with illness severity in words the night clinician can use. A list of problems without severity is not a handoff.
lines: The action list is timed: tonight, not soon.
The receiver's read-back is part of the verbal handoff even when the note exists.
A contingency, what to do if the pressure falls, is one sentence.
miss: A copied problem list with no watch item.

source.name: Starmer et al. I-PASS. New England Journal of Medicine.
source.says: Illness severity and a timed action list are required. A problem list alone does not transfer the plan.

title: An opioid agreement is not a reason to abandon the patient
lead: If you stop an opioid, you still treat the pain and the withdrawal. Stopping the prescription is not the end of the relationship.
lines: Naloxone stays on the list if the risk remains.
A benzodiazepine combination is addressed directly.
The CDC guideline does not ask you to desert the patient.
miss: Dismissing a patient from the clinic the day you stop the opioid, with no taper and no follow-up.

source.name: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids.
source.says: Clinicians continue care when opioids are reduced or stopped. Abandonment is not part of opioid stewardship.

title: Document the interpreter's name in the consent note
lead: The consent note names the professional interpreter. A family member in that blank is an incomplete consent.
lines: The language is recorded.
Questions the patient asked are in the note.
A short interpreter encounter is rescheduled if the procedure is elective and the discussion was rushed.
miss: Consent obtained via the patient's child, with no interpreter identified.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: The interpreter's identity is part of the consent documentation. Family members are not substituted.

title: Write the chaperone's name or the patient's decline
lead: For a breast, pelvic, or genital exam, the note names the chaperone or records that the patient declined one after it was offered.
lines: The exam stops if consent is withdrawn.
Each step is explained first.
A declined chaperone is not the same as an offer that was never made.
miss: No mention of a chaperone in a pelvic-exam note.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: The offer of a chaperone and the patient's response are documented for sensitive examinations.

title: A DNR order does not discontinue the antibiotics
lead: If the order is do not resuscitate, the antibiotic, the surgery, and the pain medicine stay unless a separate order stops them.
lines: Write the limits in specific words.
Ask the patient which treatments they still want.
Comfort medication is ordered even when resuscitation is not.
miss: A blanket hold on all medications because DNR was checked.

source.name: StatPearls. Advance Directives.
source.says: Resuscitation status is specific. Other treatments continue unless they are separately declined.

title: Comfort medicines are ordered before the ventilator is stopped
lead: Before a ventilator is withdrawn, order the opioid or benzodiazepine that will treat air hunger. The withdrawal order and the comfort order are written together.
lines: The intent, relief, is in the note.
A dose chosen to relieve symptoms is not an order to end life.
The family is told what they will see.
miss: Stopping the ventilator with no medication for air hunger.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Symptom-relieving medication is ordered before withdrawal of ventilatory support. The intent is comfort.

title: Put the blood-refusal on the chart before the incision
lead: A capable patient's refusal of blood is a signed order visible to the anesthesiologist and the blood bank before the operation starts.
lines: The consequence, including death, is in the note.
A surrogate does not create a refusal the patient did not make.
A child is transfused if transfusion is life-saving, even if a parent refuses.
miss: Discovering the refusal as the blood is hanging.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Refusal of transfusion is documented and communicated before surgery. It is not left as a verbal aside.

title: Emergency treatment of a child is ordered when a parent refuses
lead: If a parent refuses emergency care that would prevent a child's death or serious harm, order the treatment and notify the protective system.
lines: Explain once, clearly.
Do not delay a life-saving transfusion for a prolonged debate.
Elective care is not this rule.
miss: Holding a life-saving transfusion because a parent said no.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Emergency treatment is given to a child despite parental refusal when delay would cause death or serious harm.

title: A cesarean refusal is documented, and the patient is not taken against it
lead: If a capable patient refuses a cesarean, document the fetal risk you explained and do not write an order to proceed.
lines: Continue to offer care.
Coercion is not an order.
The note quotes the patient's words.
miss: An operative order after a clear refusal.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: A capable patient's refusal of cesarean delivery is recorded and honored.

title: Sterilization is not added to a cesarean consent in labor
lead: Do not add tubal ligation to a cesarean consent signed during labor unless a considered consent was obtained before labor.
lines: Pain and fear make that moment inadequate.
A prior antenatal consent is confirmed, not assumed.
The cesarean itself still needs its own current consent.
miss: Writing tubal ligation in the margin during a contraction.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Sterilization consent is completed before labor. It is not added under the pressure of active labor.

title: Implied consent is a note that says why you could not wait
lead: When you treat an emergency without consent, the note says what the emergency was, whom you tried to reach, and why delay was unsafe.
lines: Elective additions are not covered by that note.
Keep trying to reach a surrogate.
The note is written by the clinician who decided, not reconstructed a day later as if it were contemporaneous.
miss: A blank consent form signed by no one, added the next day.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Emergency treatment without consent is documented with the reason delay was unsafe and the attempt to find a decision-maker.

title: Recheck capacity when the sodium or the drug wears off
lead: A capacity determination is redone when the sodium, the oxygen, or the sedative changes. Do not leave a one-time note as a permanent label.
lines: The question is this decision, today.
A refusal that appears after the patient clears may be valid.
The earlier note is not deleted. An addendum says what changed.
miss: A capacity-lacking flag that follows the patient for the rest of the admission after the delirium clears.

source.name: StatPearls. Competency and Capacity.
source.says: Capacity is reassessed when the reversible cause changes. It is decision-specific and not a permanent label.

title: An against-advice departure still gets the prescription that makes leaving safer
lead: If a capable patient leaves against advice, order the antibiotic or the insulin they need for a safer exit, and document the risks you explained.
lines: A signature is ideal and is not required for the note to count.
Offer to treat the dangerous problem before they go.
Capacity for this decision is one line in the note.
miss: Withholding a needed antibiotic to punish the departure.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Bridging treatment is offered. The risks and the capacity assessment are documented even if the patient refuses to sign.

title: A POLST is placed where emergency clinicians will see it
lead: A completed POLST is copied to the record and the patient is told to keep it where ambulance crews look. An advance directive in a lawyer's office does not travel.
lines: The order and the directive are not swapped.
A capable patient can void it, and that voiding is communicated.
Inconsistent orders, full code in one place and DNR in another, are reconciled before discharge.
miss: Telling the family the living will in the safe-deposit box will guide the paramedics.

source.name: StatPearls. Advance Directives.
source.says: Portable medical orders have to be available to emergency clinicians. Advance directives stored off-site do not function as those orders.

title: Report suspected elder abuse before discharge
lead: If you suspect elder abuse, the report is made before discharge, and the suspected abuser is not the person you ask for permission.
lines: Treat the injury.
A safe destination is part of the discharge.
You do not need proof to report.
miss: Discharging a fearful older adult back to the person you suspect, with no report.

source.name: StatPearls. Elder Abuse.
source.says: The report is made when suspicion exists, and a safe disposition is arranged. The suspected abuser does not authorize the report.

title: Report suspected child abuse from the emergency department
lead: Suspected child abuse is reported before the child leaves, or the report is made and the child is kept safe until it is. A parent's objection is not a hold.
lines: Photograph and document injuries in words a later reader can see.
Treat the injury.
Do not promise the family you will keep it between you.
miss: A discharge home with a plan to think about reporting tomorrow.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Suspected child abuse is reported promptly. Parental permission is not required.

title: Remove an impaired colleague from patients before the report is finished
lead: If a colleague is impaired now, they stop seeing patients immediately. The report follows. It does not come first while they keep working.
lines: The patients already seen are reviewed.
A suspicion you cannot yet support is reported through the proper channel, not announced in the hallway.
Your discomfort is not a reason to wait.
miss: Waiting until the end of the impaired colleague's shift to say something.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Immediate risk is interrupted first. Reporting follows and does not delay removal from patient care.

title: An addendum after a complication is timed and signed
lead: After a complication, corrections are an addendum with the time you learned the fact. Do not reopen and rewrite the original note.
lines: The disclosure to the patient matches the addendum.
A late entry is labeled late.
Deleting a line is not an option the record allows honestly.
miss: Changing the original assessment after the outcome is known.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Late corrections are addended, timed, and signed. The original entry is left intact.

title: Research procedures are a separate consent form
lead: A research biopsy or an extra vial is a separate consent. It is not added to the clinical consent the morning of surgery.
lines: The patient can refuse and still have the operation.
The form says what is experimental.
The person obtaining research consent can explain the study.
miss: Adding an extra research biopsy to the surgical consent in the preoperative bay.

source.name: StatPearls. Informed Consent.
source.says: Research activities require their own consent and can be declined without affecting standard care.

title: Do not order a placebo disguised as a drug
lead: Do not order a placebo labeled as an active pain medicine. If a symptom needs treatment, order a real treatment or an honest explanation.
lines: A research placebo is a consented order.
The patient who improves on a real explanation does not need a deception.
Trust is part of the next visit.
miss: A sugar capsule labeled as a strong analgesic.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Deceptive placebo prescribing is not an acceptable order. Research placebos are consented.

title: Call the designated requester for organ donation
lead: When death is near and donation is possible, call the designated requester. Do not tie your recommendation to stop support to a yes on donation.
lines: The withdrawal decision is documented on its own.
The family is not told that stopping depends on agreeing to donation.
Your role and the requester's role stay separate.
miss: Offering to stop the ventilator only if the family agrees to donation.

source.name: StatPearls. Medical Ethics.
source.says: Donation conversations are made by a designated requester and are not a condition of withdrawing support.
